newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac sees stronger growth in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Chirac sees stronger growth in 1997.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac, delivering his traditional New Year message, forecast on Tuesday stronger economic growth in 1997.
He also said his "essential objective" was to reduce unemployment, which hit a record 12.7 percent in November.
He added that the centre-right government would go "faster and further" in cutting taxes than it had in 1996.
Chirac said that growth in 1996 had been too weak to "reduce unmployment, which is my essential objective."
"But our growth will take off and will be stronger in 1997," he promised.
He added that his government would seek to liberate the country's energies in simplifying regulations and bureaucratic red tape and "in going faster and further in cutting taxes."
France's most recent official forecast is for 2.3 percent growth in gross domestic product in 1997 after 1.3 percent for 1996.
But Prime Minister Alain Juppe said earlier this month that economic growth should be around 2.4 percent in 1997 and that this figure represented "a floor...not a ceiling."

Chirac said the government would make reducing youth unemployment a priority in 1997 and called on "every business in France, every municipality, every association to take part in this great national effort."
